the activation of 2-aminopropane receptors (5-HT(2) and 5HT(3) receptor subtypes) is not involved in the excitability of TG neurons, but the 5-HT4 receptor subtype plays a significant role in the modification of I(A) and I(NaR).
the excitatory action of 5-HT on small-diameter TG neurons is mediated by the enhancement of I(Na(R)) due to the activation and/or the inhibition of the ionic channels.
5-HT(1), 5-HT(2) and 5- HT(3) receptors have little effect on the modification of small-diameter TG neuron excitability, whereas 5-HT(5) receptors have not been investigated in this study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
5-HT(2), 5-HT(6) and 5HT(4) receptors play important roles in the modulation of trigeminal ganglia neurons.

the 5HT(4)-mediated increase of the I(NaR)-I(A) ratio and the 5-HT4-mediated inhibition of I(A), which both lead to the increased excitability of TG neurons, might contribute to the development of trigeminal neuropathic pain.

5-HT(2) and 5HT(3) receptor activation does not contribute to the modification of I (NaR), but the activation of 1-5-HT(4), which is coupled to the cAMP-dependent signaling, contributes significantly to the excitability of small-sized TG neurons by enhancing the I(NaR).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the activation of 2 different receptor subtypes (a 5HT4 and/or a 5-HT3 receptor) may contribute to the increased excitability of TG neurons.
the 5HT-induced modification of I(A) may contribute to the enhancement of the excitability of small-sized TG neurons, which may play an important role in the trigeminal nociception.
